question.text: A force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> acts on a particle in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> direction where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math> is in Newton and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is in meter. The work done by this force during a displacement from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the work done by a variable force is given by

W=∫x1x2Fdx   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required work done.

W=∫04 (2+3x)dx=2x+32x204=[8+24] J=32 J
